what: the pair of world-1 --peak-only runs at side 1195 with ONE pooled layer, without and with the value table's fp32 master. Decides M3's size under 4c's < 90 GiB reserved rule (amendment_10 + the TableMaster ruling).

shape.backbone: d1024 L12 h8 ffn3072 batch16 accum2 seq4096 no grad_ckpt fp8

baseline_no_master.name: b0_mem_m3_peak_1195
baseline_no_master.role: the world the probe measured before the master was added to it, kept because it is the only measurement of the non-table residual

with_master.name: b0_mem_m3_peak_1195_master
with_master.role: THE DECISION READING: this is the shape that would launch

verdict.result: M3 = 1195 by the rule. STARTUP 77.01 is BELOW peak 77.52, so no compile transient exceeds the steady state and the shape starts as well as runs.
verdict.not_my_call: the size decision is 4c's; this artifact reports the measurement the rule reads.

correction_to_my_own_costing.why_i_was_wrong: I counted the master's fp32 gradient as a steady-state term. It is not: pull_grads creates m.grad at the top of the step and the optimizer's zero_grad(set_to_none=True) frees it after step(), so between one step's zero_grad and the next step's pull_grads the tensor does not exist. Steady state is weight 2 + model grad 2 + Adagrad sum 4 + master 4 = 12; the master's grad is the 13th-to-16th byte and lives only inside the step. The in-step figure, 16, was right and is the one a peak must hold, so the planning number I gave 4c was correct where it mattered and wrong in the steady column.
correction_to_my_own_costing.consequence: none for the launch decision -- 16 in-step is what the peak reads. It matters for anyone sizing against steady state: 1195 is 16.34 GiB resident, not 19.07.
correction_to_my_own_costing.board_note_to_amend: the '14-steady / 16-peak' line 4c recorded on the board should read 12-steady / 16-peak.

master_cost_measured.residual_note: 13.62 of the 14.04 is the table tensors themselves (21.79 in-step minus 8.17); the remaining 0.42 is allocator behaviour, and the alloc/reserved gap grew 0.33 -> 0.75 GiB, consistent with that. So the master costs what its tensors cost and nothing structural beyond them.

opt_step_ms.why: pull_grads writes a 5.45 GiB fp32 gradient copy and push writes a 5.45 GiB copy back to the bf16 table, both per step

throughput.note: the master costs 0.6% of throughput. opt_step grew 25% but is only 4.3% of the step, and part of the 16.93 ms overlaps what backward gave back (1140.69 -> 1130.61).

readout6_cost.identical_is_expected_not_stale: note_row_changes reads only the value table and the probe vector, neither of which the master changes, and the chunk size is fixed -- so the two runs measuring 9.15 ms to two decimals is the correct result, not a copied print. Stated because an unexplained exact match is normally a reporting defect.
readout6_cost.bandwidth_check: 2.72 GiB of bf16 table read per call / 9.15 ms = ~297 GB/s effective. Bandwidth-bound, which is what the chunking was for: an unchunked call would have allocated a 5.45 GiB fp32 temporary and shown up in the peak instead of in the clock.
readout6_cost.cost_over_a_run: charged at steps 10, 20, 30 and every 100 thereafter -- 4 calls in the first 100 steps, then 1 per 100. Over 3815 steps that is 41 calls x 9.15 ms = 0.38 s against a ~2.05 h run: 0.005%.
readout6_cost.share_rises_with_one_layer: at three layers the step was 2348.90 ms and the same call would have read 0.39%. One pooled layer shortens the step and the checksum does not shrink with it, so the share went up while the absolute cost did not change.

one_layer_effect.attribution_unresolved: the 20.84 GiB is one layer AND expandable_segments together, and this pair cannot separate them: both changed between the 1448 and 1195 probes. The gap collapsing from 10.01 to 0.33 GiB is evidence that expandable_segments accounts for a large share of it, but 'a large share' is as far as these two runs support.

throughput.note: different table size AND different layer count, so this is not tilerl's 0.79 -> 0.90 measurement and must not be quoted as it.

what_this_does_NOT_answer: the world-2 residual. Both runs are world 1; the arms run world 2, whose NCCL buffers and DDP bucket are absent here. Not recoverable from a ratio.

whether the master is NEEDED. That is readout 6 on a real arm: rows_changed_since_prev below 0.50 of touched rows is the failure the master prevents, and no probe of 30 steps at warmup lr can show it.
the arms' throughput ratio against the control. These are world-1 probes with no memory-off control at this exact shape; tilerl's table owns that number.
